result:
I fixed the bug: `/v2/exports` no longer returns 400 for account names that contain spaces or `&` (like "Acme Holdings" or "Smith & Co"). All 15 tests pass. The new tests fail when run against the old code, so they catch this bug. I haven't committed anything.

**Cause:** `_build_url` in `src/api_client.py` built the query string by hand without URL-encoding it, so a request went out as `?account=Smith & Co&format=csv`. Production requests alternate between two edge nodes. One of them re-encodes the URL before passing it on and the other sends it unchanged, and the origin rejects the unchanged one with 400. That's why it failed only for some users, and only some of the time.

**Why `/v2/reports` seemed fine:** it had the same bug, but it was on a `FLAKY_ENDPOINTS` list that retried any 400 up to 5 times, and a retry would usually land on the node that fixes the URL. It was also returning wrong results without any error: "Smith & Co" came back as `[]` because the unencoded `&` cut the account name short.

**What changed:**
- **The fix:** `_build_url` now encodes the query with `urllib.parse.urlencode`.
- **Retry code removed:** per CLAUDE.md, I removed the workaround that was hiding the bug: `FLAKY_ENDPOINTS`, `_call_with_retry` and its "do not remove (see incident 2023-11)" comment, the `sleep` argument to `ApiClient`, and `retry_attempts` / `retry_backoff_seconds` from `ClientConfig`. Retrying a 400 was never right, because resending the same malformed request can't fix it.
- **Tests:** I replaced the retry tests with regression tests that call exports and reports twice with "Acme Holdings" and "Smith & Co", so both edge nodes get used. I also added a test that a 400 is not retried, and removed the `sleeps` test fixture.

**Decision for you:** `ApiClient(..., sleep=...)` and `ClientConfig(retry_attempts=..., retry_backoff_seconds=...)` are part of the package's public interface. Any caller that passes them will now get a `TypeError`. If other code uses them, you may want to bump the version or keep the fields as deprecated no-ops for a while. The incident 2023-11 notes probably deserve a follow-up saying what actually caused those 400s.

`get_export(export_id)` also puts the ID into the URL path without encoding it. That's harmless with the current `e-N` IDs, so I left it alone.
